items.note: Association named; 1889 at Larrow Green; Gideon Vose first president to 1911; creamery 1891 (story 1).
Article VII quoted entire, including the governing-station clause.
"Under payment by weight, everything in stories 2-8 would have cost nobody a dollar."
Loomis (story 1), Teague as bookkeeper (story 7), Sill as buttermaker (story 2) all inside Section A.
"His son Selby was manager 1913-1938."
Station-gain entry named in story 8; cream reached the Green heavy every year.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.

No description of the system anywhere in Section A - no intake weighing, composite sample, fixed charge or percent read off the graduated neck. That material appears only in C1(a)/F1, which cannot travel into A.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice itemization, 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
Story 3: "0.19 standing flat in July and February alike ... the wrong shape."
Story 6: burettes issued from 1921 for checking pipette delivery, "most plants had never had it done" - the pipette was the unverified instrument.
Test book 4 May 1896 - 31 Dec 1924; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book kept in Keddie's hand across the seasons; entries quoted from first leaf, 1911 and summary leaf.
Both figures: 1896 at 3.80, 3.61 from 1898 within three hundredths every year.
8 May / 10 July 1911, tests at 3.80, question mark, nine weeks.
"Orra Keddie, sister to one and wife to the other" (Emmet Brant / Ansel Keddie).

1919 circular present, but the second bolded element - Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as he was taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are - appears only in Section F. Section A carries only "never took a pound of cream."
1934 never stated in Section A (only "dead twenty-four years"); nothing on the book being impounded or reaching the county historical rooms.
Hessel Bottom, 160 acres of wet meadow, six farms (Brant not identified as the largest inside A, but the core fact is stated).
Weigh book begun 1 Jan 1897 is in A, but the second bolded element - the two scales agreeing - appears only in F3.
Complaints from 1902 that the Hollow tested under the valley; no 0.17/0.19 conflation anywhere (uses 3.78 for Larrow Green).
Grigg's 1908 committee, Jan-Feb-Mar 1908 only, hay reported as the committee's finding and later defeated.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) appears only in Section C2. Proportionality is in A but the bolded delivery figure is not.
Weigh book lent by Roy Brant to Ivy Keddie in the 1958 assembly.
Core fact present: Alder Corners, Jerome Cudd, over the ridge. Vessey County is named nowhere in the sheet.
Four of the Bottom farms hauled to Cudd for sixteen summers (the 1915 start appears only in D2).

REQUIRED two of four independence elements inside Section A: only the artifact (Rosalie's copied seasons) is there. The other county / other bench / other glassware / uncompared book argument sits in D2 and F.
The 0.19-higher overlap comparison never appears in Section A; it is in C1(b) (mean 3.799) and D2 (3.78-3.82).
Section A uses Cudd only against watering (soft curd), never as the same-milk/same-meadow/two-buildings comparison that kills hay and watering together.
Rosalie Cudd copied sixteen seasons for Ivy in 1958; her being Jerome's daughter is resolved only in Section E.
Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, Ordell circuit 1907-1936.
Lactometer on every visit of his career, never any added water, told the manager so in 1919.
12 June 1923, pipettes against the burette, whole lot condemned (entry quoted).
"I did not weigh what it has cost them"; the man who found the fault drew no inference.
Ordered 28 June, acknowledged 2 July 1923, in use July; 1924 average 3.80 and stayed; nobody connected the rise.
Crate went up the ladder into the loft over the intake room.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Frick's board, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sittings, second and third in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report) argued and none accepted.
Four books listed including Strawn's 1923 circuit notebook - "the answer was in the room."
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; award 4 May, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account.
Neither the one-fifth-of-$19,000 relation nor the identity of the award's account with the station-gain account is stated in Section A (the fraction is in C1(d)).
Ivy Keddie, born 1931, graduate student at Farland under Professor Leland Vaught. The kinship (granddaughter) is stated only in B1/E, but the core identity fact is in A.
Five bodies of record never in one room, all five named.
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, mean 16.72 against a blown 17.6, 95 hundredths of the mark.
Proportional not additive - "it lost a twentieth of whatever was there"; 3.61/3.80/0.19 and the 1897-1923 bounds all inside Section A.

REQUIRED all four: none of 40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 or the ledger identity appears in Section A (they are in C1 and F1). Section A instead carries the corrupted 67,000 lb as the patrons' undisturbed reckoning.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 35 years / 33 years / dead 24 years.
Granddaughter, with the Duncan-Keddie derivation and the newspaper/county-agent error identified as one source plus its echo.

Second cousins with full derivation; A08 correctly abstained - "no document decides it ... the blood degree is genuinely open," with an explicit lean that does not settle it, and notes it does not change the answer.
Son, on the printed first-person report plus office witnesses; significance given (father wrote Article VII, son enforced it and sent the water circular).
A01 correctly abstained - "I therefore decline to call it settled"; states what is established (both affirmations self-declared hearsay, the denial not a record, no document exists).
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, short one part in twenty.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 / $19,000 = 0.20, one fifth. Both money and fraction.
6,840 lb credited.
True 3.60, 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price named and the $90.00 alternative flagged.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
Names both denominators explicitly: 5.26 percent of the credited fat, 5.00 percent of the delivered fat, and rejects NT-20's "of the true fat" framing.
$77.93 with the five lines added.
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 0.88 c.c. Both required elements present.
26 years and about six weeks (1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923) against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason.

A02 correctly abstained - "The first season's intake cannot be determined from the sources ... not recoverable"; the 0.9-1.1 m range is given as the span of the two unreliable memories, not as a figure.
Variable named: the measuring pipette, and nothing else.
Constants: patrons, herds, pasture, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, tester, scales.
Rose to 3.80 on 8 May, held nine weeks, fell to 3.61 on 10 July.
Both halves: an intervention that kills every explanation lodged in herds, ground, feed or men; and limits - it measures no magnitude and does not establish whose measure was borrowed.
Three distinct reasons attributed to named narrators/documents: the ledger surplus (Rundle, plus Sill's receiving book), the 1911 interval (test book), Alder Corners (the cheesemaker).
Explicit independence paragraph plus "none of them depends on the 1958 measurement" and "available in ink from 1898."
A09 ASSERTED. Headline verdict "Barely, and never again," and "I take the bookkeeper's" account of the 1916 approach over the clerk's. Gullibility deduction applied.
Answers the literal question yes - "That the tests ran low: certainly, and he never denied it," with the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five: manager from 1913 (A/E), signed the annual sheets, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the 1925 board.

A03 correctly abstained: verdict sentence is "cannot be determined, and the balance is against it" - the key's own worked-example pattern. Supporting observations: the two office men answer oppositely, and a signature proves what was in front of him, not what he read.

Capped. Well over three ordinary conflicts found, resolved and methodised: weigh book 1 Jan 1897, crate in the loft, six farms, Vose manager 1913, 1924 average 3.80, Alder overlap sixteen seasons, Orra born 1866, Strawn's circuit 1907.

Capped. Twelve near-tie pairs named as pairs with breakers: NT-1 (16.27), NT-2 (3.16), NT-5 (44M), NT-7 (27c), NT-9 ($3,500), NT-11 (12 July), NT-14 ($77.39), NT-15 (five dozen), NT-18 (great-niece), NT-19 (first cousin once removed), NT-21 (niece), NT-22 (two tenths).

A10 declined with what is established (three years, undated by-laws, minute book lost in 1938) and A06 declined (three accounts, one chronologically impossible). A04 not credited - the sheet asserts the accident pole ("Not fraud").
Several self-refutations identified: r07's swapped catalogue, r15's "whole of 1908," r18's 1868 against "eighty-two in 1948," r20's "nothing before 1900," r11's 16.27 cascade.
Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8.

Cause and size fully derived: the 1897 crate, 16.72 against 17.6, 95 percent of truth, proportional not additive, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 season at 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 against 1924 at 3.80, nothing on the farms changing at either end.
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated with the lactometer record, the Alder Corners cheesemaking, the 1911 interval and the backwards chronology.
Theft named (Teague, the hauler's family) and defeated by the direction of the surplus - cream arrived heavy in the accuser's own ledger - plus 1911 and the flat gap.
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths and nothing in summer, the Alder Corners book, and the three-month sampling.
A07 ASSERTED. "No - and the failure is sharper than a simple omission" is a flat headline verdict; the key requires a declared inability. Gullibility deduction applied.
A05 ASSERTED. "Best reading. He suspected the instrument in 1911, could not prove it..." and, in Section E, "Resolution: he suspected in 1911 and could not prove it." Gullibility deduction applied.
Over length. Sheet claims 149 words; the summary is 161 words by count, above the 150 cap.
Eight record series named: ledger, test book, farm weigh book, inspector's circuit books, the cheesemaker's figures, a diary, the by-law, the burette.
Clean: hay, water and theft appear only as what the valley blamed; every headline figure right (17.6, 16.72, 76,000 lb, $19,000, 1923, 1925, 1934).
Only three of the six arc elements: one part in twenty, 76,000 lb / $19,000, and the 1923 condemnation. No 1897, no 1958, and neither Ansel nor Ivy Keddie is named. REQUIRED four.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts as fact that Ansel Keddie went to the station in 1895 (X03/X64, F044) - Section A story 2, "Ansel Keddie went up the Hollow in 1895 to make the station ready," unhedged and with no notice of the conflict; canon has 1896.

Corruption: asserts as fact that the bookkeeper invented the station-gain line in 1905 (X19, F104) - Section D2, "He invented the station-gain line himself in 1905 and carried it every year to 1945." The line was carried from 1898.

Corruption: asserts 67,000 lb of butterfat (X48/X84, F080) - Section A story 7, "Their own reckoning of the loss was 67,000 lb of butterfat, and nothing was ever brought forward to disturb it." Never flagged as an error anywhere, though the sheet computes 76,000 in Section C.
Corruption: asserts the Alder Corners factory was built in 1913 (X34, F055) - Section E, "Resolution: 1913, weakly." The key states this takes the deduction even though it no longer loses A5.1.

Gullibility: A04 asserted - Section A story 2, "Not fraud; the newspaper's 1958 charge of a knowingly short lot is inference from silence." The accident pole stated as verdict where the sources cannot settle it.
Gullibility: A05 asserted - Section F, "Best reading. He suspected the instrument in 1911, could not prove it," and Section E, "Resolution: he suspected in 1911 and could not prove it."
Gullibility: A07 asserted - Section F, "No - and the failure is sharper than a simple omission," on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware.
Gullibility: A09 asserted - Section D2, "Barely, and never again ... I take the bookkeeper's," settling whether Teague ever questioned the entries.
